learningObjective: Understand IREE's MLIR-based AOT compiler + runtime with HAL abstraction.

canonicalClaims.claim: IREE compiles input MLIR dialects (StableHLO / linalg / tosa) through target-specific pipelines into a serialized VM bytecode module (`.vmfb`) plus device artifacts; the IREE runtime executes it via a HAL supporting CPU, Vulkan, CUDA, Metal, ROCm.
nonImplications: Does not imply IREE always outperforms vendor libraries.
Does not imply IREE is a single monolithic binary.

misconceptions.claim: IREE is a Python interpreter for StableHLO.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is an AOT compiler + native runtime.

misconceptions.claim: IREE is a thin wrapper around vendor kernel libraries.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It runs a full MLIR pipeline and generates code (SPIR-V, LLVM, PTX).
Server GPUs (A100/H100) via CUDA/HIP backends are also targets.

misconceptions.claim: IREE requires a JIT compile step at every model invocation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AOT is the primary path; the compiled `.vmfb` is loaded and dispatched.

implementationFacts: Input dialects: StableHLO / TOSA / linalg / Torch-MLIR.
HAL backends: CPU (LLVM), Vulkan (SPIR-V), CUDA, Metal, ROCm.
